title: FERC rejects the core of PJM's large-load plan (Interim Resource Adequacy Service, bring-your-own-capacity); accepts the 50 MW large-load definition and a large-load registry
status: rejected in part, accepted in part

facts.accepted: PJM definition of a large load as 50 MW or more at one site; large-load registry tracking location, ramp schedule and capacity supply
facts.rejected: Interim Resource Adequacy Service (IRAS); PJM rules for 'bring your own new capacity'
facts.el25_49: Not referenced on the fetched pages. Search summaries describe EL25-49 as a separate co-location docket; not verified.

summary: FERC rejected the Interim Resource Adequacy Service package and PJM's bring-your-own-capacity rules, and accepted the 50 MW large-load definition and a large-load registry. Trade-press coverage reads the main objection as jurisdictional, with the curtailment design belonging to states.
source_title: MGRID — FERC Rejects PJM's Curtail-First Plan for New Large Loads, and Keeps Only the 50 MW Definition and a Registry
verbatim: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission rejected the core of the large-load plan from PJM Interconnection on October 9, 2026. | PJM filed the package on August 13 in docket ER26-3515-000. | It accepted only two parts. | The main FERC objection is jurisdiction, not the curtailment idea.
second_verbatim: FERC, however, rejected the Interim Resource Adequacy Service package, which made up the core of the proposal.
notes: ferc.gov news releases and orders returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so the docket and holdings come from MGRID and Utility Dive, neither of which quotes the order itself. MGRID says it did not read the order. The 50 MW threshold is confirmed by the MGRID fetch, not by the Utility Dive fetch. The brief's ER26-3515 docket is confirmed. Existing record ferc-pjm-colocated-el25-49 was not linked: no fetched page ties ER26-3515 to EL25-49.

title: FERC approves Duke Energy Carolinas transmission provisions for large-load-driven network upgrades, 4-1, Commissioner Judy Chang dissenting

facts.docket: ER26-2691 (per MGRID); eLibrary accession 20261009-3054 cited by Utility Dive
facts.terms: Rate treatment and financial security for large-load-driven network upgrades; shortfall payments for loads of 100 MW or more; new or transferred large loads pay a committed revenue contribution equal to 75% of scheduled MW for 15 years
facts.concurrences: Commissioner Lindsay See (concurrence dated Oct 9, 2026, calls it 'an incremental improvement, not a slam dunk'); Commissioner David Rosner (concurrence per Utility Dive and MGRID)

summary: FERC approved provisions of Duke Energy Carolinas' transmission tariff for network upgrades driven by large loads, including financial security and shortfall payments for loads of 100 MW or more. Commissioner Chang dissented, saying the proposal lacks meaningful financial security requirements and adequate transparency around executed large load agreements.
source_title: Utility Dive — FERC approves Duke large load transmission rules despite cost-shift concerns
verbatim: On a 4-1 vote, the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission on Friday approved
second_verbatim: The Federal Energy Regulatory Commission acted in docket ER26-2691. | A transmission customer that serves a large load must pay for at least 75% of its planned load. | The floor lasts 15 years, even if the actual load comes in lower.
chang_dissent_verbatim: She said the proposal "lacks meaningful financial security requirements or adequate transparency around executed large load agreements" (Utility Dive, truncated in fetch)
notes: Docket ER26-2691 is stated by MGRID only; the Utility Dive article cites only an eLibrary accession number. The Chang dissent is in the Utility Dive fetch; MGRID's cited Chang statement concerns a separate December 2025 Lockhart order, not this docket, so the dissent rests on one source. ferc.gov was not reachable.

company: Duke Energy Carolinas / Duke Energy Progress
title: Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress and parties file large-load tariff settlement in the NC rate-case dockets

facts.dockets: E-7, Sub 1329 (Duke Energy Carolinas) and E-2, Sub 1380 (Duke Energy Progress)
facts.filing_date: 2026-10-06 (certificate of service: 'This, the 6th day of October, 2026')
facts.signatories: Duke Energy NC; Amazon Data Services, Inc.; Andale LLC; Carolina Industrial Group for Fair Utility Rates II and III; U.S. Department of Defense and other federal executive agencies; Google LLC; Microsoft Corporation. Meta is NOT on the signature list.
facts.scope_thresholds: (a) total contract demand of 50 MW or more with expected 12-month rolling average load factor of 80% or more, or (b) total contract demand of 150 MW or more and any load factor
facts.grandfathering: Applies to ESAs executed after June 1, 2026; customers receiving service as of June 1, 2026 but later executing an ESA are excluded from the new incremental-service rule
facts.minimum_billing: Billing demand will not be less than 75% of contract demand for all demand charges in Schedule HLF (tariff exhibit)
facts.effective_date_of_tariff: Effective for service rendered on and after January 1, 2027 (tariff exhibit; subject to Commission order)
facts.early_exit: Remaining-term payment includes NPV of remaining Extra Facilities Charges and 25% of remaining minimum billing demand charges (tariff exhibit). The $587 million figure in the settlement is the 'Max' Basis for Security in an illustrative letter-of-credit table, not an exit penalty.
facts.decision: No hearing or decision date in the settlement. The Commission may 'investigate, accept, or reject the terms contained in this Stipulation, in whole, or in part.' A Commission order is required before the tariff takes effect.

summary: Duke Energy Carolinas, Duke Energy Progress and named parties filed a settlement on a large-load tariff in the NC rate-case dockets. The settlement sets 50 MW/80% load-factor and 150 MW thresholds, and a 75% minimum billing demand. It takes effect only if the Commission approves it.
source_title: Duke Energy / Parties — Agreement and Stipulation of Settlement on Large Load Tariff, Docket Nos. E-7 Sub 1329 and E-2 Sub 1380 (filed Oct 6, 2026; hosted by SELC)
verbatim: Enclosed for filing with the North Carolina Utilities Commission is the Agreement and Stipulation of Settlement on Large Load Tariff among Duke Energy — North Carolina Utilities Commission, Amazon Data Services, Inc., Andale LLC, Carolina Industrial Group For Fair Utility Rates II and III, United States Department of Defense and all other Federal Executive Agencies, Google LLC, and Microsoft Corporation.
second_verbatim: The N.C. Utilities Commission will have to approve some version of the settlement for it to take effect.
notes: Primary source: the settlement letter and tariff exhibit were read from the filed PDF after pdf stream extraction (text, not byte-verified against the PDF viewer). Verbatim above is from the letter; thresholds and 75% are from the tariff exhibit and the body of the stipulation. The brief's '75% monthly minimum billing' should read '75% of contract demand for all demand charges'. The brief's '$25M to over $587M' early-exit range is NOT supported; the $587M is an illustrative security figure. The brief's 'mid-November' decision date is NOT in the filing or in WUNC. The brief's listing of Meta as a party is NOT supported by the signature list. The Public Staff is referenced in the filing's procedural history, but is not on the signature list in the extracted text. Secondary coverage (Axios) reports the 50 MW/80% and 150 MW criteria, consistent with the filing.

title: Michigan PSC conditionally approves DTE Electric special contracts for the Google Van Buren Township data center (Case U-22058)

facts.case_number: U-22058 (per a WebSearch summary of the MPSC release; not on any fetched page)
facts.scope: Special contracts for the Google facility: primary supply agreement for electric service and a clean-capacity agreement for new energy resources and storage (per search summary)
facts.conditions: Special contracts cover generation, transmission, distribution and other costs; minimum monthly billing demand of 80% of contract capacity; 20-year contract duration; termination payment ensuring Google LLC pays at least 15 years of minimum monthly charges
facts.service_timeline: Begin taking service December 2027; maximum load December 2028 (per search summary of DTE statements)
facts.exit_payment_claim: DTE statement reports up to $2.5 billion if Google exits early and $1.7 billion in savings for other customers (search summary only; not on a fetched page)

summary: The Michigan Public Service Commission voted unanimously on Oct 1, 2026 to grant conditional approval of DTE Electric's special contracts with Google for a 1 GW data center in Van Buren Township. The commission order says the contracts must cover generation, transmission, distribution and other costs. The Commission's authority covers only the utility service; it does not decide whether the facility can be built.
source_title: Michigan Public — Google data center Van Buren Township (Oct 2, 2026)
verbatim: Michigan's utility regulator voted unanimously Thursday to grant conditional approval for DTE Energy contracts to power | ensuring the special contracts for the Google facility cover generation, transmission, distribution, and other costs | minimum monthly billing demand of 80% of the contract capacity | a termination payment that ensures Google LLC will pay for at least 15 years of minimum monthly charges
notes: The MPSC press release, the MPSC data-center consumer page and the Michigan Advance article all returned HTTP 403 to WebFetch, so the primary MPSC text was not read. The Oct 1 date is Thursday per the Michigan Public article. U-22058 and the $2.5B/$1.7B DTE figures come from search summaries only; do not publish them before reading the MPSC order or press release. The brief's 80% figure matches the Michigan Public article's 'minimum monthly billing demand of 80% of the contract capacity', but it is a contract term reported by news, not a Google statement, so do not file it as a Google Claim.
